title: Saudi Carriers Add India Flights as Indian Airlines Extend Suspensions to November 14
excerpt: Flynas is adding services from Dammam to six Indian cities and from Riyadh to three, the Indian Consulate in Jeddah said, while Air India, IndiGo and Akasa keep most Saudi routes suspended.
body:
• Flights to India are available on Saudi carriers despite the disruption: services continue from Jeddah and Madinah, limited operations have resumed from Riyadh, and Flynas has added flights from Dammam and Riyadh, per updates from the Indian Embassy in Riyadh and the Consulate General in Jeddah reported by Gulf Business.
  • Flynas's added services run from Dammam to Lucknow, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kozhikode and Kochi, and from Riyadh to Delhi, Hyderabad and Kozhikode on select dates.
  • Indian carriers remain largely suspended: Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo have extended Saudi cancellations until November 14, 2026.
  • If you hold an Indian-carrier ticket for travel up to November 14, check the airline's rebooking and refund options before buying a replacement; verify any new booking directly with the airline before travelling to the airport.

For Indians trying to get between Saudi Arabia and India, the map has split in two. Indian airlines have extended their Saudi suspensions until November 14, but Saudi carriers are still flying — and adding capacity. According to an update from the Indian Embassy in Riyadh and the Consulate General of India in Jeddah, reported by Travelobiz and Gulf Business, Saudi carriers continue to operate flights to India from Dammam, Jeddah and Madinah, and limited operations have resumed from Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport.

The added flights

Flynas has announced additional flights on nine city connections: from Dammam to Lucknow, Mumbai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kozhikode and Kochi, and from Riyadh to Delhi, Hyderabad and Kozhikode on specific dates. The Consulate shared the update as Indian diplomatic missions work with airlines to improve connectivity, with particular attention to Umrah pilgrims affected by the disruptions, which followed an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. One-stop connections through other international airlines' hubs are a further option.

The Consulate's 24-hour control rooms in Jeddah and Makkah remain operational for Indians needing assistance, Travelobiz reported, and tour operators have been encouraged to use the expanded options for pilgrims.

What is suspended, and until when

The Indian side of the corridor is a different picture. Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo have extended cancellations on Saudi routes — including Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah — until November 14, 2026, and Akasa Air has extended its own suspensions, according to Travel and Tour World's summary of the airline announcements. Airlines are offering one-time complimentary rebooking, subject to availability, for affected passengers holding confirmed tickets issued on or before October 30 for travel up to November 14, the same report said.

What to do if you are travelling

Three checks, in order. First, if your booking is on an Indian carrier for travel before November 14, treat it as suspended until the airline tells you otherwise, and take the rebooking or refund rather than duplicating the trip. Second, if you need to travel, price the Saudi-carrier options from Dammam, Riyadh, Jeddah or Madinah — and confirm the seat and schedule directly with the airline before making airport transfers, as availability depends on the date. Third, if you are an Umrah pilgrim or are assisting family members who are, the Jeddah and Makkah control rooms are the official assistance channel. Schedules in a disruption change faster than aggregator listings; the airline and the mission updates are the sources to trust.
